title: Kata independent adversarial review record
description: One adversarial pass over a sealed revision, executed in a clean context. `status: recorded` carries what the adversarial reviewer attempted and found; `status: waived` records an explicit decision to proceed without it. Whether the pass really ran in a fresh context is attested by the executing agent — kata can gate on the attestation and on the brief it was given, not on the host's session.

candidateFreezeSha256.description: The CandidateFreeze this pass certified (§7.4): the content snapshot plus the semantic contract it answered. Stamped so a completed certification can be reused for the freezes it is still valid for, instead of being expired by a revision id that moves on any re-seal.

codeManifestHash.description: Content identity of the revision's code paths only (C2). Stamped beside manifestHash so a code-scoped verdict can outlive a governance-text edit; absent when the split cannot be derived, in which case a code-scoped binding refuses to match.

governanceManifestHash.description: The governance-text surface at the time of this verdict (§22/§24). A text-only edit expires what this surface was verified for, and nothing else.

instrumentManifestHash.description: The declared-instrument surface at the time of this verdict (§24.4). Editing a declared instrument expires the instrument surface only — not the pass about the deliverable.

baseManifestHash.description: For a delta pass: the manifest hash whose change surface this pass measured.

scope.description: What the pass covered: full means every path was re-derived; delta means only changedPaths were.

deliveredFacts.description: What this pass read, as facts rather than text: one entry per path it drew a conclusion from. The hash is taken from the content when the record is written, so a later round can tell a fact that still describes the file from one that does not.

elapsedMs.description: How long the pass took, reported by the executor. Recorded so a delta pass can be compared with the full pass it narrowed (design §11: the saving had never been measured).

toolUses.description: How many tool calls the pass made, reported by the executor. The turn loop, not the CPU, is what a pass mostly costs (design §1), so this is the first term of that cost to become visible.

mode.description: How the round was framed (M2): verify lists the author's claims, cold lists none. The platform rotates the default and records it here, because the next rotation reads it.

hypotheses.description: The judgement basis: what the reviewer asserted, over what, by which method, and what it observed. The verdict is derived from these by kata; `verdict` is a display field that may not contradict them.

receipt.description: The executor's report that fresh context was a *capability* rather than an assertion. Host-authored, measured and bound: it arrives on its own channel (`--receipt-file`) rather than in the reviewer's result body, and the gate refuses a record whose receipt does not bind to the issued request by nonce and hash, or whose capabilities omit what the node requires. Authorship separation is process and tool policy, not cryptography — a receipt a single-user machine could forge is out of scope here.

executor.description: Provenance for this receipt. On a subagent round the telemetry is relayed by the calling session, so the identifiers are what let an auditor check the numbers against the platform's own record.

platform.description: Which host produced this receipt. Provenance, never a gate criterion: capability is the contract, and naming a platform must not read as a requirement.

sessionId.description: The session the round ran in, so the platform's own record of it can be found.

completionReport.description: The platform's completion line verbatim — what the relayed figures were transcribed from.

toolCalls.description: Measured by the executor, or null where the platform could not report it. Null is not zero: an unmeasured figure must not be fabricated into one.

outputBytes.description: Measured by the executor, or null where the platform could not report it. Null is not zero: an unmeasured figure must not be fabricated into one.

tokens.description: Measured by the executor, or null where the platform could not report it. Null is not zero: an unmeasured figure must not be fabricated into one.

truncations.description: Measured by the executor, or null where the platform could not report it. Null is not zero: an unmeasured figure must not be fabricated into one.

toolUses.description: How many tool calls this attempt took (§18.7). Per attempt rather than per pass so a costly hypothesis is visible while it runs, which is when the decision to stop is made.

falsifier.description: The check that must redden under this defect: a declared selector, a command, or the observation that refutes the claim. The brief asks every finding to carry one, so the write path must accept it.

impact.description: What else the repair will touch: the other call sites, the fixtures, the second derivation of the same concept. An observation the pass already holds — not a repair recipe, which would make this pass a second author of the fix. Measured cost of its absence: one repair broke eleven fixtures across six files and the suite was the only thing that said so.

classInstances.description: Where else this same defect exists, as the pass observed it. A finding names one location; the class it belongs to usually has several, and a repair that fixes one instance leaves the rest for the next round to find. Measured cost: two repairs on this line fixed one derivation of a concept with four producers, and each time the next round found the next producer.

reproduction.description: How the review confirmed the finding, carried forward from the review record so a reader can tell a reproduced finding from one whose test is missing.

findingOrigins.description: How many of this pass's findings were caused by the previous repair (design §F3): recorded so the marginal cost of fixing is on the same account as the cost of finding.

usage.description: What the round cost, recorded so the loop's price is a fact rather than an impression. Measured on this line: seven rounds cost 351,864 / 658,523 / 347,000 / 400,000 / 875,572 / 510,836 / 1,073,271 tokens and produced 7 / 0 / 5 / 5 / 0 / 7 findings — the two most expensive produced zero because they never wrote a record, so cost and yield are not correlated and the number exists to be discussed rather than driven down.

wroteTests.description: The test files this pass created. A pass may not leave one behind, and declaring none is the ordinary case — the field exists so the check refuses self-contradiction rather than inferring authorship from the filesystem, which cannot answer it.

readTests.description: Test files this pass read and argued from, which it did not write. Declared because no filesystem fact distinguishes a test a pass read from one it wrote — the file exists either way — so the record states it and the guard checks the record against itself.

replacedCreatedAt.description: The createdAt of the record this one replaced in the node's slot. Recorded at write time because the replacement relation is not derivable from a record's fields — a replacement inherits the revision or keeps it while findings accumulate.

replacedFindingIds.description: The ids the replaced record held — the other half of its identity, because createdAt is not unique and a count is not stable.

replacedBy.description: Which event produced this write: 'append' when a finding was added to the record already in the slot, 'round' when a fresh pass replaced it. Recorded here because an append overwrites the live record's link to the round it replaced, so the consumer cannot infer the shape from the timestamps.
